checks: Each attached primary PDF was inspected in full once and its local SHA-256 matched papers.primary_file_sha256.
All five records already carry the appropriate true-exclusion status mental_health; none has extraction fields or population rows. Their exact batch membership is retained rather than replaced.

S2236 is a cross-sectional DASS-21, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and Epworth Sleepiness Scale comparison of 12 youth and 10 adult Chilean cerebral-palsy footballers; it reports psychological and sleep outcomes, not injury or illness surveillance.

S2238 is a 3-week observational low-energy-availability, diet, and body-composition study of 11 female National Premier League soccer players; injuries only appear as a participant-exclusion reason and it reports no injury outcome denominator, count, rate, burden, or severity.

S2285 is a phenomenological, semi-structured-interview study of eight Turkish Amputee Football Super League athletes about anxiety and coping; injury is an anxiety theme rather than a measured injury outcome.

S2305 is a cross-sectional EAT-26, DOS, BES, and bioimpedance assessment of eating-disorder/orthorexia risk and body perception in 51 elite/first-division soccer players; injury only appears in an eligibility criterion and there is no injury/illness outcome extraction.

S2308's stored primary PDF is internally a 26-page study of physical-activity barriers among 531 Filipino college students, not the cited pre-competitive-anxiety paper on young female soccer players. Its SHA matches the stored live attachment, so the attachment/citation mismatch is documented rather than silently repaired. The citation title and abstract still support the existing mental_health classification.
No Tabs 1-10 fields, derived values, structured rows, populations, or status corrections are staged. Consequently there are no field IDs to validate and no structured dual-write payload.
